title: The Remonstrants' view is tolerable
source_text: LXX. Nihil ergo pejus hac in parte sentiunt Remonstrantes illis qui Lutherani dicuntur; ac proinde cum Reformati communionem horum non refugiant, sed ultro eos ad pacem & concordiam fraternam invitent, non debent Remonstrantes propter hoc doctrinae caput, si nihil gravius errent, a communione sua repellere; sed eorum hac in re sententiam habere pro tolerabili, & quae pietati perniciosa non sit.
pass_a_gloss: LXX. Therefore the Remonstrants think nothing worse in this part than those who are called Lutherans; and accordingly since the Reformed do not shun communion with these, but of their own accord invite them to peace & brotherly concord, the Reformed ought not, on account of this head of doctrine, if they err in nothing more grave, to repel the Remonstrants from their communion; but ought to hold their opinion in this matter as tolerable, & as not pernicious to piety.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXX. On this point, then, the Remonstrants think nothing worse than those called Lutherans. The Reformed do not avoid communion with the Lutherans; they even invite them, unasked, to peace and brotherly concord.

So, unless the Remonstrants err in something more serious, the Reformed should not shut them out of their communion over this head of doctrine, but should regard their opinion on it as tolerable and not harmful to piety.
